correctness.rationale: Feng proves VR_{<=3}({0,1}^n) is a finite wedge of b4(n) four-spheres and b7(n) seven-spheres with both multiplicities positive for n>=5. For pairwise separated cubes C_k={3k,3k+1}^n, coordinate clamp is 1-Lipschitz in l1 and hence induces a simplicial retraction from the entire lattice Rips complex onto each cube. On any other C_j it is constant, so induced positive-degree homology maps vanish. Every singular simplicial cycle is a finite chain and maps to zero under all sufficiently remote cube retractions. Therefore direct sum of cube homologies has left inverse and splits in lattice homology. Since Z^n has countably many simplices, homology rank at most aleph0, and the free split sum makes exactly aleph0 in degrees 4 and 7. No assertion of torsion-freeness or vanishing elsewhere. Independently verified clamping inequalities on mixed-sign examples; universal proof uses elementary Lipschitz and finite-chain arguments.
residual_risks: Split free subgroup does not determine possible torsion or other homology; countability is for simplicial finite chains, not infinite formal chains.
